page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.32xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs (64 physical cores) utilizing the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 4096 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding 32 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is provided via a 3800 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with the passmark CPU score and stress-ng multi-core tests placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 6660.4 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 302.32 GB/sec for large-block reads. Database operations are a key strength, as demonstrated by a strong rating in Passmark database operations and Redis SET performance of 106.84 million operations per second. However, single-core performance remains average, and large-scale LLM text generation (70B model) is weak at 2.76 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

Given its massive memory footprint and high-speed local NVMe storage, the x2iedn.32xlarge offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads. It is highly cost-effective for enterprise-grade relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, large-scale data analytics, and electronic design automation (EDA). The inclusion of local NVMe SSDs and 100 Gbps networking minimizes the need for external storage overhead in data-intensive environments.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, it features 128 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, paired with 4096 GB of DDR4 RAM and 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The instance delivers 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks show strong multi-core capabilities, high memory bandwidth, and excellent database execution, with Redis SET operations reaching 106.84 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is average, and the lack of a GPU limits its efficiency for large LLM text generation. This instance is highly suited for large in-memory databases, data analytics, and memory-heavy enterprise applications where high RAM-to-vCPU ratios and fast local storage are critical.
